- When sentiment is positive (≥0.06) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add 0.5–1.0 point upward adjustment if sentiment turns neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility in early periods (e.g., 1–5 days after spike); apply 0.3–0.7 point upward bias if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.06) and price is stable, model tends to underestimate; add 0.2–0.5 point upward bias to avoid underreaction.
